subsystems.name: Cryptographic discovery
subsystems.role: finds every place encryption and signatures are used, since you cannot migrate what you cannot see.

subsystems.name: Post-quantum key establishment
subsystems.role: replaces the RSA and elliptic-curve key exchange whose security a future quantum computer would break.
parts: hybrid mode combining it with a classical curve

subsystems.name: Post-quantum signatures
subsystems.role: keeps device and software authentication unforgeable.

subsystems.name: Protocol integration
subsystems.role: carries the new algorithms through the protocols infrastructure actually speaks.

subsystems.name: Hardware roots of trust
subsystems.role: signs keys and boot images in silicon so the algorithms cannot be swapped by an attacker.
parts: embedded secure elements with limited memory

subsystems.name: Key and certificate management
subsystems.role: re-issues, rotates and revokes an entire estate of certificates.

subsystems.name: Quantum key distribution (optional link layer)
subsystems.role: an alternative that derives keys from physics rather than mathematics, over dedicated fibre.

buildSteps.title: Build a cryptographic inventory
buildSteps.detail: Scan every network link, server, firmware image and protocol to record what algorithms, key sizes and certificate lifetimes are in use across operational technology as well as IT.

buildSteps.title: Rank what must move first
buildSteps.detail: Anything whose data must stay secret for decades, or that is expensive to replace, is prioritised — long-lived grid and industrial equipment especially.

buildSteps.title: Choose hybrid deployments
buildSteps.detail: Run a post-quantum algorithm alongside a classical one in the same handshake, so security holds if either is later broken.

buildSteps.title: Integrate into protocol stacks
buildSteps.detail: Implement the algorithms in TLS, IPsec and certificate libraries, respecting the tight packet-size and memory limits of embedded devices.

buildSteps.title: Test performance on real devices
buildSteps.detail: Larger keys and signatures cost bandwidth and compute; measure on substation gateways and meters before rollout, not in a lab only.

buildSteps.title: Re-issue the PKI
buildSteps.detail: Regenerate certificate authorities and device certificates with post-quantum signatures, and push them out through controlled maintenance windows.

buildSteps.title: Deploy in stages
buildSteps.detail: Roll out to external-facing systems first, then internal, then the slowest control networks with the longest hardware lifetimes.

buildSteps.title: Monitor and retire
buildSteps.detail: Continuously scan for regressions or forgotten classical endpoints, and phase out the old algorithms once every peer supports the new ones.

prerequisites.why: NIST published its first post-quantum standards in 2024, giving implementers fixed targets.
many operational systems hard-code their cryptography and cannot be updated without replacement.
keys must be generated and stored in certified hardware, and support is still arriving.
substation and industrial devices can run for decades with no practical path for a firmware change.
commercially available over limited fibre distances, but needs dedicated links and trusted nodes.

pathway.milestone: post-quantum standards published; hybrid key exchange already switched on in mainstream browsers and some VPNs
pathway.unlocks: a proven, interoperable algorithm set to build against.

pathway.milestone: full post-quantum TLS, IPsec and certificate rollout across enterprise and utility networks
pathway.unlocks: resistance to recorded traffic being decrypted later.

pathway.milestone: refreshed PKI and hardware roots of trust, aligned with national-security migration deadlines around 2030 and exclusive use by the early 2030s
pathway.unlocks: forgery-resistant authentication for grid and financial control traffic.

pathway.milestone: retirement of RSA and elliptic-curve cryptography, plus quantum repeaters for long-distance QKD
